abstract: Cooperative game theory answers canonical questions on payoff allocation (Shapley, Owen), interaction attribution (Grabisch-Roubens, Faith-Shap), and coalition formation and stability. None answers a fourth question that arises whenever players carry known, overlapping group tags fixed independently of the game: how should a player's standing be distributed across the groups it already belongs to? We call this membership attribution, formalize it, and give a complete characterization of its solution. The direct, ratio-based answer is provably invalid whenever a player's group-level signals have mixed sign --- a common, structurally unavoidable case. We propose a restricted-domain softmax construction instead, and prove that, for any player satisfying a precisely defined richness condition on the group structure, it is the unique such map, up to a temperature parameter, satisfying five requirements. A sixth requirement fixes the sign of this temperature; a seventh, shown independent of the rest via an explicit counterexample, forces one shared temperature across all eligible players. A worked example on an exact cooperative game confirms the applicable requirements numerically and shows the construction degrades gracefully, valid but uninformative, when a player's evidence fails to distinguish between its groups.

title: A Characterized Softmax for Distributing Standing Across Multiple Affiliations
